subject: Data retention & PII handling — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Carter <john.carter@acmefinance.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmefinance.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Data retention & PII handling — post-call follow-up

Hi John / Priya —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and the immediate asks I captured: 

- PII handling: your security team requests that any user content classified as sensitive PII be excluded from long-term storage (prefer 0-retention for request/response bodies that contain PII)
- Audit/logging: you still need operational logs for troubleshooting and compliance, but want retention shortened to 30 days for logs that may include request identifiers
- Data residency: all processing and logs must reside in us-east regions; key material must be customer-managed via KMS
- Proofs: you requested a copy of our SOC2 artifacts and a completed security questionnaire (attached below)

Next steps proposed: 
1) We’ll circulate a proposed retention schedule and mapping for the endpoints discussed (see proposed_retention_matrix.pdf)
2) Our solutions engineer (Rafael) will confirm what we can set to TTL=0 versus redaction/censoring options for PII
3) If that looks acceptable, we’ll put together an exception request that legal can sign off on and route into the contract (if needed)

Can you confirm that 0-retention for user content + 30-day logs is the right approach for your team, or flag any specific endpoints that must be treated differently?

Attaching: security_questionnaire.docx (completed draft)

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: John Carter <john.carter@acmefinance.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmefinance.com>, Acme Finance Security <security@acmefinance.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention & PII handling — post-call follow-up

Camila —

Thanks for the recap. Correct on the high level:
- 0-retention for any request/response bodies containing full PII (names, SSNs, account numbers)
- Logs/trace data: 30-day retention max; we can redact any direct identifiers but need request IDs and timing for incident triage
- Data residency: US-East only; we cannot replicate to other regions
- KMS: yes, customer-managed keys required for encryption at rest

Two quick questions:
1) Does Redwood support encrypting logs with our KMS when logs are stored for up to 30 days?
2) Do you have an option to redact PII at the ingestion layer vs. storing and deleting later (we prefer never to store full PII if possible)

Attaching our internal security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_acme.pdf) — some of the answers will overlap with what you provided.

If you can get Rafael to outline the technical approach (redaction vs TTL=0) we’ll be able to move this into a legal review quickly.

Best,
John Carter
Director, Platform Security | Acme Finance
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Data retention & PII handling — post-call follow-up

Forwarding John’s reply and Acme’s asks — can you weigh in on what’s feasible and a recommended approach? Key constraints: 0-retention for PII-containing bodies, 30-day logs, US-East only, CMK for KMS.

Rafael — can you confirm the options below and what we should propose back to Acme? Please include any changes to performance/cost: 
- Option A (Preferred by customer): Ingest-time PII redaction (pattern-based + model-assisted) so no PII gets persisted. For redaction we can return a tokenized placeholder in responses. Tradeoffs: small latency increase on ingest (~15–35ms avg), lower storage costs, simpler legal stance.
- Option B: Store request/response bodies with TTL=0 (immediate delete) and aggressive KV/cache eviction. For LLM inference we need to ensure KV cache is not persisted beyond request; runtime change may be required. Tradeoffs: lower runtime changes but requires proof-of-deletion and audit hooks.
- Logs: keep structured operational logs (request ID, timestamps, model variant, route) for 30 days. We can encrypt these with CMK; need to confirm log pipeline with CMK integration (Log ingestion -> S3-like store encrypted with CMK, access logging).

I attached a first draft of the proposed_retention_matrix.pdf (will clean up once we confirm). Rafael — can you draft language we can surface to legal for an exception (if needed) and confirm any blockers? Neha — will you lead the legal path for an exception once engineering confirms technical feasibility?

Thanks —
Camila

Attachment: proposed_retention_matrix.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Carter <john.carter@acmefinance.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmefinance.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention & PII handling — post-call follow-up

John / Priya —

Thanks for the clear direction. Per our internal review here’s the proposed next steps and options: 

1) Technical approach (Rafael to confirm in-line):
   - We recommend Option A (ingest-time redaction) as the lowest-risk approach: removes PII before any persistence. Expected impact: +15–35ms request latency on average; minimal change to runtime architecture.
   - Option B (TTL=0 on stored bodies) is possible but will require a runtime change to ensure KV caches are ephemeral and a verified deletion/audit flow; timeline 4–6 weeks for engineering work and additional validation.

2) Logs and encryption:
   - We can retain structured operational logs for 30 days only and configure encryption-at-rest using your CMK (you provide the key and cross-account policy).
   - We will not replicate logs outside us-east and will disable cross-region backups for this account.

3) Legal/commercial:
   - If you prefer Option A we can include a data handling addendum and operational appendix confirming redaction behaviors and audit controls.
   - If you require a formal 0-retention exception (Option B), Neha (CC’d) will lead the exception review and propose contract language — this will likely be added as an attachment to the Master Services Agreement.

Next steps: Rafael — please confirm final technical notes and any cost delta. Neha — once Rafael confirms, can you prepare the exception/addendum draft and we’ll route to Acme legal for signature?

Camila — can you coordinate a 30-minute technical sync with Acme and Rafael for Thursday?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
